decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch that builds directly on the firm's core spraying systems, management is likely to keep it because it fits existing capabilities and any modest market traction can still be justified as normal ramp-up.
Its own product page, field-test reference, and close fit to the firm's established injection business create visible commitment and sunk-cost pressure to continue rather than withdraw it.
Because this is a product line with several models built on the firm's existing offer, the breadth of investment and strong strategic fit make withdrawal within a year unlikely.

Fire protection flow monitoring has been publicly presented on its own page and supports the firm's stated move toward future-oriented, more interoperable solutions, so management would likely persist with it.

Although it is the newest and least publicly established launch, it is still close to the core two-component spraying business, so management would probably retain it and attribute any weak early results to its short time on the market.
